definitions.explanation: Small particles of burning material that fly through the air from a fire. Also used figuratively for trouble or conflict that spreads to or affects uninvolved parties.

examples.japanese: {火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}い{上|あ}がった→舞い上がる：06043_maiagaru⟧。
examples.english: Sparks flew up into the air.
The wind carried sparks all the way to the neighboring house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{降|ふ}りかかる→降りかかる：28386_furikakaru⟧{火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{払|はら}わ→払う：00535_harau⟧⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: You have to brush off the sparks that fall on you.
examples.notes: A proverbial expression meaning one must deal with trouble that comes one's way.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used figuratively in the expression ⟦{降|ふ}りかかる→降りかかる：28386_furikakaru⟧{火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{払|はら}わ→払う：00535_harau⟧⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧, meaning "you must deal with trouble that comes your way" — i.e., you cannot ignore problems that affect you even if you did not cause them.

The figurative use of {火|ひ}の{粉|こ} refers to the fallout or collateral effects of someone else's conflict or scandal reaching you.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}ぶ→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧: sparks fly
- {火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧: sparks dance / swirl
- {火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧: brush off sparks (deal with trouble)
- {火|ひ}の{粉|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}りかかる→降りかかる：28386_furikakaru⟧: sparks rain down (trouble comes one's way)
